e: Three activists are sentenced to up to seven years' imprisonment on charges of violating national security over their commemoration of the Tiananmen Square massacre in 1989.
The United States imposes a 12.5% tariff on Hong Kong, citing the presence of alleged forced labour in the supply chain.
Authorities announce the seizure of 230,000 suspected counterfeit 2026 FIFA World Cup-themed merchandise valued at $20 million.

Football players Brian Fok and Luciano are convicted along with a betting agent for running a match-fixing gambling operation that covered some 30 matches of the Hong Kong First Division League from 2021 to 2023.

The Central Criminal Court in London, United Kingdom, charges two British Chinese nationals of violating the National Security Act for spying on diasporic Hong Kongers on behalf of the China-appointed Government of Hong Kong.
The Hong Kong Court of Appeal overturns Jimmy Lai's conviction for fraud in the subletting of office space.

Kwok Yin-sang, the father of exiled pro-democracy activist Anna Kwok is convicted of making financial transactions involving "fugitives" as part of the national security law following an attempt to terminate an insurance policy on his daughter. He is sentenced to eight months' imprisonment on 26 February.
Activist Jimmy Lai is sentenced to 20 years in prison following his conviction of colluding with foreign forces.
A backpack containing 51 million yen (USD330,000) in cash is stolen in a robbery outside a currency exchange shop in Sheung Wan.
